questions.prompt: What is the safest way to choose TypeScript compiler settings?
options: Align the configuration with the installed compiler, target runtime, libraries and bundler, then type-check the project.
Copy a tsconfig from another project without checking its runtime.
Assume every option works in every TypeScript version.
Disable all strict options before inspecting diagnostics.
questions.answer_key: Align the configuration with the installed compiler, target runtime, libraries and bundler, then type-check the project.
questions.explanation: Compiler settings describe environment assumptions and change across versions; validate migration and build behavior.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “TypeScript 7 Compiler Performance”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with native compiler architecture and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with native compiler architecture and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Native compiler architecture”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “TypeScript 7 Compiler Performance”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check parallel build controls, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume monitoring build speed, memory use, and watch-mode behavior is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check parallel build controls, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Parallel build controls”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
